question: Do Gated Linear Unit variants used in place of the ReLU/GELU feed-forward sublayer improve the Transformer?
contributions: Extends the GLU family with ReGLU, GEGLU and SwiGLU (and Bilinear) and proposes them as Transformer FFN layers
Tests them in the T5 transfer-learning setup on pre-training perplexity and GLUE, SuperGLUE and SQuAD

method.summary: Replaces the T5-base FFN (two matrices) with GLU-variant FFNs (three matrices, d_ff cut from 3072 to 2048 to match parameters and compute). Each model is pretrained 524,288 steps on C4 span filling without dropout, then fine-tuned once on a mixture of GLUE, SuperGLUE and SQuAD.
method.task: T5 span-filling pretraining then multi-task fine-tuning on language understanding

datasets.name: C4
datasets.split: heldout shard of C4 for log-perplexity
datasets.preprocessing: inputs of 512 tokens, outputs of 114 tokens containing multiple deleted spans

datasets.name: GLUE
datasets.preprocessing: examples-proportional mixture with SQuAD and SuperGLUE

models.name: T5-base with FFN variants (GLU, Bilinear, ReGLU, GEGLU, SwiGLU)

other.d_ff: 2048 for GLU variants (3 matrices), 3072 for baseline (2 matrices)

training.lr_schedule: inverse-square-root, decayed linearly for the final 10 percent of steps
training.steps: 524,288 pretraining; 131072 fine-tuning; 65,536 for the 4 variability runs
training.dropout: none in pretraining; 0.1 on layer outputs, FFN hidden layers and attention weights in fine-tuning
training.seeds: four models per architecture trained 65,536 steps to measure inter-run variability; one run of the full 524,288 steps

other.finetune_runs: one run on a mixed task set (departs from Raffel, who fine-tuned separately)

inference.samples: best dev score of any checkpoint recorded during fine-tuning, per task

metrics.name: heldout log-perplexity
metrics.definition: on the span-filling objective, heldout C4 shard

eval.protocol: Single full run per architecture; std in parentheses from four 65,536-step runs; best checkpoint per task on dev sets, so selection on the reported split.

availability.code: based on the T5 codebase; no release stated

evidence.quote: we reduce the hidden layer to dff = 2048, so as to maintain the same parameter and operation counts as the base model

results.claim: The Raffel et al. baseline with identical architecture is notably worse, which the author attributes to dropout in pretraining
results.setup: T5-base encoder-decoder (12+12 layers, d_model 768), C4 span-filling pretraining, parameters and compute matched, heldout-shard log-perplexity; Raffel et al. 2019 reported SQuAD dev EM
results.note: Author's attribution to dropout is a belief, not tested
results.table: Table 4, row [Raffel et al., 2019], column EM

results.claim: The author offers no explanation for why gated variants work.

limits: Author offers no explanation: 'We offer no explanation as to why these architectures seem to work'
Fine-tuning results are noisy; one fine-tuning run per model, best checkpoint chosen on dev sets
Single pretraining run per architecture at 524,288 steps; variability only measured at 65,536 steps
Only T5-base scale (12+12 layers, d_model 768); no larger models
Some downstream tasks favour baseline GELU or ReLU (e.g. CoLA, CB)
Comparison with Raffel et al. confounded by dropout: author removed dropout in pretraining

terms.definition: component-wise product of two linear projections, one first passed through a sigmoid
